I am writing this review after weeks of trying to resolve a serious security issue directly with support. I have been playing on BC.Game for nearly a year, reaching Silver VIP status with over $158,000 in total wagered volume—yet this is how they treat a loyal player. 

On June 15, my account (Synista, UID 95470688) was compromised despite having active Google 2FA enabled. An unauthorized third party got into the account, unstaked my tokens, played high stakes games, and managed to drain $940 USDT out of a $2,499.80 USDT total asset liquidation.

I acted immediately by locking down sessions and changing my credentials, but support still locked the account. I went through their entire KYC re-verification process to prove identity, and my account access was finally restored on July 15. However, BC.Game flat out refuses to take responsibility for the security bypass or refund the $940 USDT that was taken while 2FA was active.

To make matters worse, that unauthorized $2.5k withdrawal completely ruined my backend account metrics. Because their automated system logs that theft as a massive payout, my weekly drops, monthly bonuses, and VIP cashback rewards have been severely cut down. Management refuses to reset or fix these stats, leaving me penalized every week for a breach that happened on their platform.

On top of that, I sent a formal email to support requesting a full lifetime transaction CSV export to audit my account, and they have completely ignored it. The stress of gathering evidence and fighting brick-wall support reps for weeks has been exhausting.

I have already logged a formal regulatory complaint with the Anjouan Gaming Board and filed a police report (ACSC Ref: CIRS-20260702-209). I am posting this here so other players know how even established VIPs are treated when security failures occur.

UPDATE (28/07/2026) in response to BC.Game:

BC.Game’s boilerplate reply completely ignores their platform’s glaring security and risk management failures:

1. Complete Failure of Automated Fraud Flags: A brand-new external withdrawal address was added to the account. A large withdrawal request was made, canceled, and then immediately split into three smaller transactions sent in rapid succession to that newly added address. On any secure platform, introducing a new wallet address combined with rapid, broken-down withdrawals triggers an immediate temporary lock or manual security review. BC.Game’s automated risk detection failed to trigger a single flag or delay.

2. Bypassed Security Controls: Claiming "third-party access" conveniently glosses over how their system allowed high-risk payout pattern changes while 2FA was active on the account.

3. Backend Metric Corruption: BC.Game refuses to address their system error. By logging these stolen funds as a voluntary personal cashout, they ruined my Silver tier metrics, suppressing my weekly bonus drops and loss cashbacks.

Helping restore basic login access after their automated systems let a high-risk payout pattern execute unchallenged is not customer service.

Fix the metric bug, restore my Silver tier account stats, and take responsibility for your fraud system's complete failure. And pay back what was stolen from me.

I'm going to leave what I consider a final, honest review of Winna. I decided to give them an extra star because there are some aspects of the platform that make it unique, but there are also concerns that I cannot ignore.

First of all, the most important point: do not blindly trust their Originals. My friend group consists of eight players, and together we recently surpassed 1 million rounds on Dice, mainly because it is one of the easiest games to wager on at scale.

Tracking results was much harder than it should have been because the live statistics tracker has been broken for roughly two months. When playing three rows simultaneously, it only records the top row correctly. Conveniently, this is also the only row that appears to behave somewhat normally. As a result, we had to manually record our wager amounts and profit/loss figures after every batch of spins.

Based on our records, the effective house edge we experienced on Dice was not close to the advertised 1%. It appeared to be somewhere between 1.8% and 2%. Most of us ended up losing roughly twice the amount that would be expected under a 1% house edge. On a sample size this large, that is extremely difficult to explain through variance alone. Even on much smaller sample sizes, such a deviation would be extraordinarily unlikely if the actual house edge were truly 1%.

Their Blackjack was even worse. We originally wanted to play a much larger sample, but after more than 10,000 hands we stopped because the results felt unusually unfavorable compared to our experiences on other crypto casinos. In our sessions, the dealer appeared to make 20 or 21 far more frequently than expected, and our aggregate results translated to a loss rate of around 10% of total wagered volume. This is something I have never encountered on any other crypto casino.

Remember that a provably fair system does not tell you what RTP (return to player) a game runs on. They can design Blackjack to be 90% RTP and Dice to be 98% RTP, and the provably fair system will still confirm that the outcomes are correct. This is why releasing the source code alongside a provably fair system is a must, so users can verify that the house edge matches the number being claimed.

Most casinos send me the source code once I ask for it, but Winna does not. They say it is proprietary, even though there is nothing proprietary about it when everything is fair and transparent. By refusing to fulfill this request, they only create more suspicion. On top of that, the complaints team ghosts me whenever I ask about it.

The last thing that has to be mentioned is the rain system. The rain is not strictly random. Our friend group of eight constantly participates in rain events. With around 100 participants and seven winners drawn per raffle, the probability of at least one of us winning should be roughly 45%. In reality, however, every single day we only won around 20% of the rains. Meanwhile, there are users who individually win more rains every day than all of us combined.

Honestly, I understand the idea of rewarding the most active users or those at the biggest loss. However, since rain requires wagering, I believe there is a moral obligation to be transparent about how the rain system works and which factors influence a player's odds. Even when I confronted support about this, they insisted that everyone has equal odds, despite the owner and an admin already confirming in chat that other factors are indeed used to reward the most active players.

If they become more transparent about the actual house edge of their Originals and the specifics of the rain system, they would deserve significantly more stars because, apart from those concerns, it is a good casino with some genuinely unique features.
